title: Attention Is All You Need
venue: 31st Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS 2017)
problem: Sequence transduction tasks, specifically machine translation and English constituency parsing.
method: The Transformer, a model architecture based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.
datasets: Wall Street Journal (WSJ) portion of the Penn Treebank
key_results: Achieved 28.4 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-to-German (improving by over 2 BLEU) and 41.8 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-to-French, establishing a new state-of-the-art with significantly lower training costs.
limitations: Reduced effective resolution due to averaging attention-weighted positions; requires task-specific tuning for some applications.
future_work: Extend the Transformer to other modalities (images, audio, video); investigate local, restricted attention mechanisms for large inputs.
key_claims: The Transformer is the first transduction model relying entirely on self-attention.
The model is more parallelizable and requires significantly less time to train than RNN or CNN-based models.
The Transformer generalizes well to other tasks like English constituency parsing.
